text.p: - Open confrontation in the State Duma between Russia's security chief, Alexander Lebed, and Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov over the Chechen crisis proves that the ruling authorities are far from united.
- The new aggressive style demonstrated by President Boris Yeltsin yesterday in his radio address and television appearance was probably inspired by the president's chief of staff, Anatoly Chubais.

- With a wide range of potential interests, Lebed presents a double danger for the president's entourage -- if he resigns he may become a powerful opposition leader, if he stays he may shake up others' positions.
- The future of the peace process in Chechnya now depends to a great extent on the readiness of the negotiating parties for compromise.
- The public images of a number of Russian ministers is built on their apparent secrecy. This is also characteristic of the new information policy declared by the top authorities.
- The sick president had to rise from his bed to counterbalance the positions of Lebed and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
- After almost two years of war in Chechnya, there are still ways to establish peaceful relations between the breakaway region and Moscow.
